one_liner: Kotlin's WasmGC compiler backend; JetBrains' 2023 charts show 1.25-2.5x faster than Kotlin/JS output on most macro benchmarks.
what_it_does: Kotlin/Wasm is a backend of the Kotlin compiler that turns Kotlin code into a WebAssembly module plus an .mjs loader, through the wasmJs (browser and Node) and wasmWasi (standalone VM) targets of a Kotlin Multiplatform Gradle project. It is in Beta per the Kotlin docs and is the web target of Compose Multiplatform. Common Kotlin code compiles to it unchanged; JavaScript interop goes through external declarations restricted to JsAny subtypes and a fixed set of built-in types, which is stricter than Kotlin/JS.
how_it_is_fast: Kotlin classes and arrays become statically typed WasmGC structs and arrays managed by the engine's garbage collector, and Int, Long and Double arithmetic maps to native Wasm i32/i64/f64 operations, so the engine runs ahead-of-time typed code rather than speculating on the types of Kotlin/JS output. Production builds are post-optimised with Binaryen's wasm-opt (the harness pins Binaryen 116 in 2023 and 129 today). The largest gains are on allocation- and pointer-heavy code (List, a recursive linked-list benchmark, about 2.5x), not on string handling.
when_to_use: CPU-bound Kotlin code you already ship as Kotlin/JS (object graphs, recursion, collections, simulations): 10 of 12 are-we-fast-yet benchmarks ran in 39-80% of the Kotlin/JS time in JetBrains' chart.
Compose Multiplatform web UIs, where Wasm is the web target and JetBrains' chart puts it at about 2x faster than the Kotlin/JS build (156-181% of JVM time vs 315-399%).
Sharing one Kotlin codebase across JVM, Android, native and web, when your users run Chrome or Chromium 119+, Firefox 120+ or Safari 18.2+.
Server-side or plugin use in standalone Wasm VMs through the wasmWasi target (the benchmark harness runs it on Wasmtime with -W gc,exceptions,function-references and on WasmEdge).
when_not_to_use: String-heavy work such as parsing or text processing: the JSON benchmark (a string-only parser) took about 174% of the Kotlin/JS time.
Tight floating-point loops that the JS JIT already handles well: Mandelbrot was level (about 102% of Kotlin/JS).
Audiences on older browsers: Safari before 18.2 is not supported, and Chrome before 119 needs a Kotlin release older than 1.9.20 plus a flag.
Code that crosses the Wasm/JS boundary constantly (DOM-heavy logic, many small calls into JS libraries): interop types are restricted and the boundary cost is not measured in these charts.
Decisions that need current numbers: the only published results are 2023 Alpha-era screenshots without hardware or engine details; re-run the harness on your Kotlin version and engine.

integration.form: compiler target (Kotlin Multiplatform wasmJs / wasmWasi via the Kotlin Gradle plugin); output is a .wasm module plus .mjs loader
integration.dependencies: Kotlin Gradle plugin (multiplatform); an engine with WasmGC and (legacy or new) exception handling; Binaryen for optimised production builds
integration.min_toolchain: Kotlin 1.9.20+ (final WasmGC encoding, per the Kotlin docs); the benchmark harness now pins Kotlin 2.3.20-RC; Gradle
integration.platforms: Chrome/Chromium 119+, Firefox 120+, Safari/WebKit 18.2+, Node.js (harness pins 26.2.0), V8 d8, SpiderMonkey shell, JavaScriptCore, Wasmtime and WasmEdge (wasmWasi)
integration.thread_safety: not documented in the sources read
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — the same common Kotlin code builds for both targets, but it is a separate target with stricter JS-interop rules (external declarations limited to JsAny subtypes and selected built-in types), needs WasmGC-capable engines, and is still Beta

gotchas: Cross-host baseline in the chart's own harness: the build script committed with the screenshots (a82a6cb, Kotlin 1.9.20) runs Kotlin/JS under nodejs() on Node 21.0.0-v8-canary202309167e82ab1fa2 and Kotlin/Wasm under d8() on d8 11.9.125 (plus both on a 2023-09-21 SpiderMonkey nightly shell); it has no browser runner, while the Kotlin docs say the results come from Google Chrome, so which run produced the chart, and whether both sides ran in the same V8 host, is undocumented.

CD, Havlak, JSON, nBody and Mandelbrot sit in the slowMacro configuration: one measured invocation (iterations = 1, iterationTime = 1 ns) after 5 warm-ups in 2023 (10 today), so those five bars rest on a single sample per target; the fast set uses 5 x 50 ms iterations. The chart also does not say whether it shows Dev or Prod builds, or the plain or Binaryen-optimised (wasmOpt) Wasm variant.

Open issue #30 (2026-10-05): the WasmEdge and Wasmtime benchmark tasks do not depend on the tasks that build the wasmWasi binaries, so after a clean build they fail, and otherwise a stale .wasm from an earlier build can be benchmarked silently and distort results.

The README's run instructions (wasmBenchmark, wasmOptBenchmark, -Pkotlin_version=1.8.0) describe the 2023 'wasm' and 'wasmOpt' targets, which the current build script no longer registers; it now builds per-engine tasks such as wasmJsFastMicro_Wasm_Prod_WasmEdgeBenchmark and loads a prebuilt kotlinx-benchmark 0.6.0 plugin jar checked into the repo.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Kotlin/Wasm when the code is already Kotlin or Compose Multiplatform; its 1.25-2.5x over Kotlin/JS on most macro benchmarks is in the same range as J2CL's WasmGC result (about 2x on the Sheets worker) and above wasm_of_ocaml's early 10-20%. Scala.js's Wasm backend is the equivalent choice for Scala code, and MoonBit is a new language rather than a backend for existing code.
verified_claims_summary: JetBrains' December 2023 chart (Kotlin 1.9.20 Alpha-era harness; the committed build ran JS on a Node 21 V8 canary and Wasm on d8 11.9.125; no CPU stated) shows Kotlin/Wasm taking 39-80% of the Kotlin/JS time on 10 of 12 are-we-fast-yet benchmarks (1.25-2.5x faster), about 102% on Mandelbrot and about 174% on JSON. A second chart from Compose's bench_with_kwasm branch (Compose 1.5.10-dev-wasm01, Kotlin 1.9.20-RC, browser targets) puts Wasm at 156-181% of JVM time against 315-399% for Kotlin/JS, about 2x faster than JS; all values are read off PNGs.
status_note: The Kotlin compiler (Apache-2.0, 53.5k stars) is actively developed with Kotlin/Wasm in Beta, and the benchmark repo is maintained (last commit 2026-10-07, harness on Kotlin 2.3.20-RC, V8 15.0.45, Node 26.2.0), but the published charts have not been refreshed since 2023-12-07.
